text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan clarifies that a solution to the Cyprus dispute should be found before accession to the European Union.
- The Canadian edition of "Time" magazine describes Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash as "diabolical" and says it will need a miracle worker to solve the dispute splitting the island.
- The education ministry has a long list of teachers who have applied to work in afternoon education institutes.
- The Americans do not see any spectacular developments on the Cyprus issue in 1997. They believe the crunch time will be after 1998, according to diplomats.
- The Turkish side is cultivating a climate of tension to undermine the forthcoming direct talks scheduled to take place between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders next month.
- Members of parliament complain the media ignores most parliamentary debates. They prefer to screen soaps instead, said one MP.
- Parliament is ready to hike the levy charged on the public for the state-run Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation while industrialists, pressure groups and consumers are hotly opposed to it.
- Rauf Denktash sets as a condition for a solution to the Cyprus problem recognition of his breakaway state.
